sentiment.rationale: The document reports a strong quarter with revenue up 8% YoY and EPS up 29% YoY, but forward guidance is largely reaffirmed rather than raised. Full-year 2025 expense guidance was raised to ~$84 billion 'at the high end of the previous range,' and NII ex-Markets is expected up ~4%, which is a modest upward revision. However, management's tone is confident but not exuberant, and the 2026 RoTCE target of 10-11% is described as a 'waypoint, not a destination,' indicating a longer-term view rather than an immediate upgrade. The score is mildly positive due to the expense guidance raise and confident forward language, but not higher because the revenue and EPS beats are backward-looking and the core guidance changes are incremental.

summary.revenue: Total revenues, net of interest expense for 2Q25 were $21,668 million, up 8% from $20,032 million in 2Q24. Excluding divestiture-related impacts, revenues were up 9%.
summary.eps: Diluted EPS for 2Q25 was $1.96, up 29% from $1.52 in 2Q24.
summary.guidance: Full year 2025 expense guidance raised to ~$84 billion, 'at the high end of the previous range.' NII ex-Markets expected up ~4%. 2026 RoTCE target of 10-11% reaffirmed as a 'waypoint, not a destination.'
summary.margin: Efficiency ratio for 2Q25 was 62.7%, improved by 340 bps YoY from 66.1% in 2Q24. Net interest margin (NIM) was 2.51% in 2Q25, up 10 bps from 2.41% in 2Q24.
key_risks: Higher cost of credit: 'Citigroup cost of credit of $2.9 billion increased 16%, driven by a higher net build in the allowance for credit losses (ACL) related to deterioration in the macroeconomic outlook in the current quarter relative to the prior-year period and a net ACL build related to transfer risk associated with client activity in Russia.'
Non-accrual loans increased 49% YoY to $3.4 billion, driven by idiosyncratic downgrades in Markets and California wildfires impact on Wealth mortgage loans.
Higher severance costs: 'higher severance of approximately $400 million, primarily related to the realignment of the technology workforce.'
Macroeconomic uncertainty: 'deterioration in the macroeconomic outlook' cited as a driver of higher credit costs.
key_opportunities: Services revenue up 8% YoY, described as 'crown jewel' with continued market share gains.
Markets had its best second quarter since 2020 with record second quarter for Equities.
Wealth revenues up 20% YoY with solid growth across all three lines of business.
Investment Banking fees up 13% YoY, with Advisory up 52% and ECM up 25%.
Transformation progress: 'streamline processes, drive automation and deploy AI.'
Capital return: 'Returned ~$3.1 billion in the form of common dividends and share repurchases.'

management_tone.label: confident
management_tone.justification: CEO Jane Fraser said, 'We reported another very good quarter and continue to demonstrate that our strong results are sustainable through different environments.'

The guidance raise is modest (expenses at high end of range, NII ex-Markets up ~4%), and the strong backward-looking results could be seen as already priced in.
